summary: Convincing Stone Age materials, distinguishable everyday roles and an excellent Chief silhouette. Approval is held back by exposed base clothing, rigid lower garments and a caravan leader whose foreign identity is too dependent on small details.
problems: The Hearthkeepers show conspicuous red/green areas at the shoulders and neckline that read as underlying shirts rather than skin or hide. Coverage must work on both avatars.

The Chief's broad hip-mounted skirt box bridges both thighs. The Hearthkeeper's long, rigid front/back panels also need walking clearance; these garments currently read as boards rather than overlapping hides.

The caravan leader shares the residents' brown palette and the Chief's pale tooth-collar vocabulary. The small shells and mostly concealed decorated bedroll do not establish a clearly foreign mammoth-herding culture at stream scale.

The Gatherer's green identification is concentrated on the front, while several other distinguishing details sit below the waist. Strengthen shoulder/top-view cues rather than relying on details that shrink or disappear from the gameplay camera.
fix: Flintworker of the Sinew Seam: Preserve the topknot, asymmetric hide and three pale seam stitches. Check exposed shoulder edges for underlying shirt geometry on both avatars; retain a short, separated apron rather than extending a solid skirt across the legs. Overlapping-Grass Gatherer: Carry the green grass mantle over the shoulder tops and onto the upper back as a few broad, overlapping pieces; preserve the basket and avoid adding fine fringe. Hearthkeeper in the Folded Shoulder Hide: Suppress the underlying shirt or cover its visible neckline and shoulder edges with fitted skin/hide geometry. Keep the large pale shoulder fold, but shorten the rigid hip panels and separate the lower overlaps so each leg can swing without intersection. Young Ridge Scout: Preserve the bare torso, single feather and short loincloth; keep this the lightest silhouette. Verify the skin overlay fully conceals the default shirt and test spear/head clearance during movement. Chief of the Great Branched Antlers: Preserve the antlers, skull staff and broad mantle—the office already reads clearly. Replace the thigh-spanning skirt box with a short hip wrap and separate overlapping lower flaps; test the cape against both legs. Far-Roving Shell-Cowl Mammoth Herder: Make the cowl a broad, contrasting grey-fur silhouette with three oversized ivory shell discs around its upper rim. Raise the strapped bedroll enough to show beyond the shoulders, and replace the generic straight collar teeth with a compact paired mammoth-tusk motif. Keep the hood lower than the Chief's antlers and use hide, sinew and bone fastenings.
